column6: Your Review
blah blah blah
Goofy guy. Super friendly. Knows his stuff though and expects you to as well. Great teacher in the plane and thorough in the debrief.
Is a super new IP. She is very nice in the brief, come prepared and she doesn't ask a lot of questions. Is pretty quiet in the plane, she wants to see you succeed. "Fly good, don't be dumb"
column7: Very chill on XC and great to fly with. Hands off (unless you need help), just ask. Will let you mess stuff up and fix it. Know your knowledge for the brief and you will have a great lesson.

column6: Stoic in the while your briefing, initially comes across serious. Overall, super willing to teach and is a great instructor. Thorough in the debrief. Will ask a lot of questions in the brief and gets excited when you know the answers, definitely a positive reinforcement kinda guy.
column7: Chill instructor, asked questions about the NWCs. Very helpful in the air and is willing to teach. Took an hour to debrief because he wanted to go through everything in a lot of detail which I appreciated

column6: Quick and to the point in the brief, doesn't like to waste time. Really fun to fly with, super patient in the plane and it a great teacher. Watch out for a beer fine over something really small.
column7: Onwing - Genuinely cares and wants you to learn the most out of the flight. Iron the brief out and you'll jump right into the plane asap. Semi concur on the beer fine, he hates the easily fixed mistakes ie: not setting CDI or resetting bugs. Don't let the small stuff slip because you feel youre doing well overall and you'll have a great flight

column6: Very patient in the plane, good teacher. Is a new IP. A little hard to talk to, but overall is a very nice person and understanding. SUPER LONG DEBRIEF
column7: Good owning instructor. Know your ADB, exterior inspection, NWC's. Is patient, however just know your stuff and you'll do fine. Debrief takes a long time, but you get to know what to work on for the next flight.

column6: Asks a lot of questions in the brief and drives most of the brief. Is super fun to fly with a good instructor and will give you a good confidence boost.
column7: Concur. Has some great USMC experience and will extend the debrief to help you think about your career. Loved to fly with him. He nerds out about fuel management and would love if you did too.

column6: Flying with him is great. Brief… know your NWC's as well as knowing the system you're briefing inside and out.
column7: Have your NWCs down, will stare at you and wait. Doesn't matter if your EP has 11 of them. Have them all. Fine in the flight. Grades the flight fairly.

column6: In my experience if you show you know what you're talking about he will talk more in discussions then you. Don't be afraid to ask questions. Will let you know if you're wrong and not in a condescending way. Has a give a fuck factor.
In my experience, super relaxed and asks the important questions. He's not there to expose any unimportant knowledge, very practical and honest in his feedback.
column7: Good instructor with relevant feedback. Super chill in brief and in the plane.

column6: Relatively relaxed in the brief, but can become a demon in the plane. Genuinely a good dude though and teacher when he's out of the plane.
column7: Offwing - Super relaxed in the brief.  Pretty laid back in the plane as well.  Super fun to fly with and gives great advice during the debrief.
column8: He was super nice in the plane and really took time to teach things especially in the pattern. It was a bad hop overall personally and he hit me pretty hard on grades even though he said I was on pace during my 4202 flight. Overall most of that was on me and he was chill.

column6: He gets a bad rep because he can come off as harsh in the plane but overall, he prioritizes safety. He told me after an O/I that he turns off most of his emotions the second he gets in the cockpit so he can focus entirely on the flight, so his criticisms can seem harsh but he really is trying to help. Even if he yells at you in the plane once you land he will be very complimentary on what you did well and what you can improve upon.

Know your procedures and NWC (Not verbim). He will give you time to rember these if you are struggling, but he seriously will unsat you if dont know the procedures and MOST of the NWC. If you make it to the plane, he is amazing to fly with, a great teacher, and honest grader.

Know your stuff in the brief, really helps for the rest of the flight. Sometimes wants to get into the weeds with discussion but it's not with a "gotcha mindset" she genuinely wants you to understand and prepare you for future flights.
column7: Absolutely can confirm on the getting prepped for future flights, I had her for a warmup after I was out of the plane for a bit and I was just not myself. Did a lot of things wrong, but she asked questions that are the exact format you'd get on a checkride and I wasn't able to answer them easily (FAM42XX Block) and I have modified my study regime and how I think about certain things like the ADB and Preflight

column6: Super nice and fun to fly with, adheres hard to cts and doesn't grade too generously, however won't below mif even if you mess up
column7: I have been below-MIF'd by him for relatively minor things (e.g. one missed ATC call) but otherwise concur

column6: He knows FTI, Natops, SOP, etc… inside and out, but understands we won't be on his level of knowledge. He asks a lot of questions, and would rather you say "I don't know" than try and guess. Overall flying with him will be a great experience.
Is a newer IP and is great for instruments. Call sign is "Radio" so make sure to get those coms down.

Brief:
You’ll brief in his office, not at the whiteboard, so bring a printout. He’ll stare at you the whole time—don’t let it throw you. He might widen his eyes mid-brief just to see if it messes with you. Stick to your plan and practice try to stare back and don’t get rattled. For QODs, go deeper than just filling in the blank—he’ll probably ask follow-ups about systems from NATOPS.

In the plane:
Super chill in the T6 and a great instructor. Doesn’t do the whole “helmet fire” thing. He won’t overload you, but be solid on comms and respond quickly when things are directed at you, absolutely don't cue your mic and go "ummmm".

Debrief:
Very thorough and detailed. Only downside is there’s so much feedback you’ll need to prioritize/triage what to fix first. Honestly though, it’s a good problem to have. You’ll know exactly what can be improved upon for next time. Grades fairly as well, there is not a single grade I recieved from him so far that I thought wasn't 100% correct.

If your scheduled for a COPC:
Should be the same vibe. If you get him, don’t stress—just prep well using what’s here and go crush it. He went through one himself when he was here.

Endure. Speaking for the FAM side especially early on if you come knowing your stuff in the brief you will have a good time, She doesnt shake hands for some reason idk. Biggest tip is good attitude and be respectful, sounds crazy but I pity the fool that gives her any lip. In the plane its rough because she is heavy on the controls. Unholy amounts of control pressure from her.
column7: Feels like she doesnt trust me to fly the plane straight and level. Doesnt help she is a ground school instructor. Knows the 3710 like the back of her hand and will not let you leave the debrief until you also know it. Also, never IMSAFE out of a flight or sim just because of gouge. Nobody became a great pilot without experiencing all ends of the spectrum. The point is for you to learn and she will ensure that you do. Suffer the pain of discipline AND regret.
column8: She grades fairly but kinda treats you like a kid. Generally thinks you're more overwhelmed than you are. She's a really nice person and I think a Tactical IMSAFE is a little extra... Cares about teaching and fixing your weak spots. She's very approachable and if you have any questions or irks she's really accomodating. Come prepared for the brief

column6: Brief: Did not care at all. Told me to skip my NATOPs brief and we just glanced at weather. Mildly briefed. Fun and chill in plane and helpful. Epic reservist.

Awesome in the airplane, hardly touches the controls at all unless to demo. In the brief, very relaxed, but wants to make sure you know the material/flight profile. Very thorough and helpful with the debrief. Honest grader. Overall, incredibly chill, show up knowing what you need to know and have a good event.

column4: Silent and Chill, semi mif monster
column6: Very laid back in the brief, will let you figure it out if you make a mistake instead of jumping your ass. In the plane he's pretty quiet but will give good demos if you're struggling. During the debrief he doesn't give exact feedback comparative to your gradesheet so I would wait on your grades before making assumptions about the flight. Overall a chiller and good to fly with.
column7: Also a very experienced T-6 Pilot, he instructed NFO's in Pensacola flying the T-6A. He's a very good IP to ask questions about the aircraft and techniques on how to do things well.

column6: New IP. Funny guy, lot of energy, super helpful. Very very stingy giving any 5s but reluctant to give 3s too
column7: Great flight with him for FAM42XX block, we flexed a ton to get all the things done we needed to during the flight and went outside the normal boundaries of contacts flights due to WX and massive traffic volume in the area. Ended up earning a 5 on Mission Planning/Execution due to being able to flex so much and stay cool the whole time.

column6: Really into EPs, Limits, and NWC in briefs. Get out of the brief, and he's chill in the airplane. He is a good teacher and genuinely cares about your success. His tips in the airplane are helpful. Debriefs are good and he tells you where to improve. Won't officially say but will challenge you to a staring contest while you are briefing.

Reservist, pretty quick in the brief, prioritizes getting to the aircraft. Asks some questions during the exterior inspection. Does a lot of good coaching while flying. Grades well and overall an insightful and pretty chill flight.

Flies for Southwest. Priorities are "have fun, be safe, learn something." Great with answering questions in the plane and will help you out if you ask. A little quiet and has a bit of a rbf but is a good IP to fly with.
Genuinely helpful and likes discussing things in depth. Enjoys answering hypothetical questions. Very willing to help out in the plane as well.

In the brief, he was chill but very much about getting it done as soon as possible. Not sure if it was just my day, but we did the discussion items after the flight. As you're going to the airplane, he quizzes you on the preflight. Nothing out of left field. In the airplane, very chill. I didn't feel him aiding the controls at all. He might sound stern in the airplane when he's telling you something to look out for; however, he is also quick to give you a compliment when you've done something well. If he sounds stern, don't let it get to you because it's just a comment. It'll literally pass in seconds. Fair grader overall. The debrief was helpful.

Brief was super laid back. He did have me brief wearing all of my flight gear so just a heads up. If there's anything you want to work in particular, let him know and you'll tailor your flight accordingly.  In the airplane, really chill gives usefull advice/tips/coaching. I'm pretty sure he said "meow, meow,meow" during GXs. Debrief was helpful, he has 2000 hours in the T-6 and did the Checkride for Maj Kuchinin. He has a dry sense of humor and is sarcastic, so just keep that in mind with his comments in the airplane/debrief. He means no malice.

Knows the CNAF and Natops extensively so just keep that in mind. Chill in the Brief, will ask you what coaching style works best for you and will apply that in the airplane. Chill in the airplane and debrief. His debriefs are in-depth and helpful. Just get ouf of the brief and have a good event.

Maybe its cause he's my onwing but I feel he really cares about you learning to fly and understanding things rather than trying to get you into the weeds of discussion items. Tends to take controls a good amount, even when I felt it wasn't really needed but otherwise, fun to fly with and a great guy overrall.
column7: Not his onwing and can confirm, very chill. Really cares about teaching and helping you improve.

column6: Really cool to fly with, also super knowledgeable about the plane. Very good instructor. I learned a ton when flying with him and is fun to brief with. Played the rolling stones out of his phone when walking to the plane.

Makes sure you know what is going on in the planned flight profile. Very practical in what is expected of you. In the plane is very complimentary and will tell you when you are doing well. Very easy to keep track of what you need to improve on in the flight. There is zero ambiguity in your grades. He will tell you what you need to improve upon and tracks how you are doing mid-flight. HOWEVER, is more of the mind that if the SNA feels comfortable with what they have done and they meet CTS, he will not make you redo it for a better grade. Overall, it was a very productive and positive flight as long as you get into the brief and know your discuss items. Has more than 1000 hours in the T-6B and knows his stuff but do not be intimidated by that because he will openly admit that he makes mistakes and he can and does. As long as you show up with a good idea of what you are doing and the profile, he will work with you on stick skills.

NATOPS Wiz. Big on checklists and wants FWB and applicable NOTAMs printed for the brief. At least for early events wants to teach and will do so during the brief. During FAM check will fail MFDs and is big on exterior inspection. Have a paper/notebook for the debrief.

Brief: Standard NATOPS, he ended up briefing me on discussion items even though I came prepared. Asked maybe a few questions. He recommended Griffs Gouge on Youtube for instrument flying. He handled most coms in the plane and was super fun to fly with. One of my favorite flights of primary so far. Highly recommend.
Very quiet and laid back in the brief and in the plane. Overall had a great time flying with him. Loves to talk about the C130!

Tries to be as hands off as possible and will let you mess up to an extent. He will give you positive reinforcement and is a good teacher. I left feeling more confident, however, he does not grade very generously

Not sure if it was because it was an aero flight but overall very fun flight and good teacher. Show up with good knowledge of procedures and discuss items. He really likes fast ground ops, so the quicker you are the better and I think it sets a great tone for the rest of the flight.
column7: Haven't flown with him but this doesn't at all match what others say about him.
column8: most people meet him it's their worst days of primary, and he is the grim reaper when it comes to that. however, he is an intelligent guy and gets a lot of students grief for it (he unsatted me once in contacts)

column6: He's with CNATRA.Very laid back and fairly quiet in the brief and flight, forgiving of simple mistakes and helps you learn from them without making you feel like an idiot. I got assigned to brief with him earlier than when my standby was supposed to be, so I was feeling less prepared than I would have liked but it turned out to be a great flight. 10/10 would fly with him again.

column4:
Chill in plane, somewhat tough grader for I4XX

Quiet/Chill
column6: I flew an event with him, plan was changed to a Tango-3 due to bad weather, the flight itself didn't seem too bad and the debrief wasn't too bad either, however I was hammered on the gradesheet. I asked another student who had him for I41XX block too and also agreed that he grades super rough for I41XX block events. Admittedly Tango-3's are tough especially for a early inexperienced instrument student, however I do think my grades were lower than other IP's would've given. (Update flew with him again, grades were far better the next time, but went on a more standard instrument profile and was able to perform better.)

Had a great experience, very nice in the plane, but it was a check so very quiet in the plane. Will still answer dual concurrence and any questions you have as long as it relates to the flight. Pretty reserved.
Chill in the plane but dont expect alot of small talk. Grades fairly and will give you opportunities to attempt manuvers multiple times.

column4: Chill to talk to, MIF monster grader
column6: Says fuck a lot like it's a sentence enhancer. Beer is Coors Banquet, the tan can. Very pointedly went down and MIF'd every item.
New STUCON O, Very good IP, interested in knowing about you. Really works to make sure you succeed.
Very nice guy, looking to teach and not give you a ton of shit.

Flew with him on a weekend so take this with a grain of salt. He's a reservist so expect to fly even if weather looks a little weird. Took a bunch of time in the brief to look over weather since we had a bunch of bad weather coming in. We were able to stay legal although we had to change of flight plans. Briefing was pretty easy, standard brief. Be prepared to talk about every point in the brief and you'll be good to go. For instruments we did a Tango 3 and stayed local. He took controls and let me setup for my approaches for almost every approach which made things a bit easier. Standard instrument flight
Flew FAM 4200, great in the plane, very knowledgeable and a good teacher

Hilarious in the brief, will make jokes, has a lot of T-6 hours so he trusts you alot with the plane and will give you a longer leash because he knows his limits with the aircraft. His debriefs are long, and if it looks like a weather cancel and he doesn't have another flight after he will sit you down and encourage you to ask questions about primary, i.e. what's expected of you and what he would focus on knowing if he was you.

P-8 guy. Loves instrument events. Among the quickest briefs I've ever had for a flight, in instruments expect standard NATOPS, and glancing at the discuss items, won't correct you but will add on if he thinks there is something important that you missed. Very communicative in the plane, and very reassuring. Very helpful on teaching techniques for instruments.

Nice guy, pretty relaxed in the brief (cut my hydraulics system explanation short and just had me skip to the next topic). Can be a nit picky on some things (ie wants you to point out and explain each part while doing the exterior inspection), but overall very nice and helpful in the brief and plane. Grades very fairly, but he expects you to know your stuff.

New instructor from the FITU. Expect to run through the whole brief and all discuss items. He loves to quote specifics from the FTI so be prepared to talk specifically about things straight from the FTI. Doesn't say too much in the plane. Will let you mess up hoping that you correct it. Don't be afriad to talk through your thought process on point to point, etc. He was a really nice grader giving lots of 4 and some 5s on things I did well. You'll be chilling if you fly with him
